name: turn
comment: The chat's turn record (app/src/PrismTurn.lex.tex): what its person said to the Prism as one W3C EMMA 1.0 document, and the turn as one W3C PROV-N document (the person and the Prism as agents, the turn as an activity that used the prompt and each thing the reply drew on, the reply generated by it and derived from them, the turn informed by the one before). The guest is built from PrismTurn, PrismEmma and PrismProv, so a record is judged by the same checkers that hold the Recommendation's EMMA documents and W3C's PROV constraint cases. 'record' and its lines (base, now, after, prompt, reply, cited) answers the EMMA document, a line end and then the PROV-N document, or 'refused: ' and why; nothing is answered that either checker faults. 'check' and a record answers 'accepted', or 'refused: ' and the standard it breaks. 'examples' are the acceptance vectors: each a 'check' of a record put together from W3C's own documents, an EMMA document of the Recommendation as the emma guest's vectors hold it and a PROV-N case of W3C's constraint suite, with the verdict W3C's case carries (PASS accepted, FAIL refused). 'sources' names the specs those bytes are taken from, each pinned there by SHA-256.

gaps.why: No authoritative source gives the expected answer of 'record': EMMA and PROV define what a well-formed record is, not which record a turn of this chat makes. So no 'record' request is an acceptance vector; what holds for every 'record' answer is that both checkers accepted it inside the guest before it was answered, and the cases under 'shape' only show the request grammar. Which PROV relations a chat turn should carry (used, wasDerivedFrom, wasInformedBy) is this model's reading of PROV-DM; ISO 24617-2's dialogue act and its dependence relations are not yet in the record.
